common_name: Little Lime Punch Hydrangea (Compact Pink-Red Aging Panicle Hydrangea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun to partial shade; Little Lime Punch keeps the compact size of Little Lime but was selected for a deeper, faster color shift as the panicles age through the season.

directions: Little Lime Punch is a compact panicle hydrangea that opens the same fresh lime-green flower panicles as its parent Little Lime, but ages through a more pronounced rosy-pink-to-red flush by late summer and fall, giving a bolder two-tone color progression on a plant scaled for a smaller border or foundation planting. Sturdy stems hold the flower heads upright without staking, and because it blooms on new wood it can be pruned hard in late winter without sacrificing the coming season's flowers. Plant in moist, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun to partial shade, and water deeply during dry spells for the fullest panicles and the most vivid late-season color change.

common_name: Fire Light Tidbit Hydrangea (Miniature Panicle Hydrangea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun to partial shade; Fire Light Tidbit is the smallest selection in the Fire Light panicle hydrangea line, well suited to a container or the front of a mixed border.

directions: Fire Light Tidbit is a true miniature panicle hydrangea, staying under 2-3 feet tall while still producing the same sturdy-stemmed, upright white flower panicles that age to deep pink-red typical of the larger Fire Light selections. Its diminutive size makes it one of the few panicle hydrangeas practical for a large container, small foundation bed, or the front edge of a border, without sacrificing the reliable, strong-stemmed flower display the series is known for. Plant in moist, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun to partial shade, and prune, if needed, in late winter, since it blooms on new wood and tolerates a hard cutback without losing the coming season's flowers.

common_name: Wee Bit Grumpy Hydrangea (Dwarf Reblooming Deep Blue-Purple Mophead Hydrangea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Wee Bit Grumpy blooms on both old and new wood, so it reliably reflowers through summer even after a late frost damages the previous season's buds.

directions: Wee Bit Grumpy is a dwarf, reblooming mophead hydrangea staying compact enough for a large container or small foundation bed, producing rounded flower heads that read as intense deep blue in acidic soil or purple-pink in more neutral to alkaline soil, following the same pH-driven color shift typical of macrophylla hydrangeas. Because it flowers on both old and new wood, a late spring freeze that damages the previous season's buds does not prevent a strong summer rebloom. Keep soil consistently moist in partial shade, since the leaves wilt quickly in dry heat, and prune only lightly to remove dead wood, since heavy pruning sacrifices the earliest old-wood flowers.
sources: North Carolina State Extension — Dwarf Reblooming Hydrangea Cultivars
Clemson Cooperative Extension — Hydrangea Selection for the South

common_name: Limelight Prime Hydrangea (Compact Improved Lime-Green Panicle Hydrangea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun to partial shade; Limelight Prime is a more compact, sturdier-stemmed improvement on the original Limelight, needing less staking to hold its heavy flower panicles upright.

directions: Limelight Prime carries the same fresh lime-green flower panicles that made the original Limelight one of the most popular panicle hydrangeas ever introduced, but on a somewhat more compact plant with stronger, more upright stems that better resist flopping under the weight of the large flower heads. The panicles age to soft pink and then tan through fall, extending the season of color well beyond the initial green flush, and because it blooms on new wood it can be pruned hard in late winter without sacrificing the coming season's flowers. Plant in moist, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun to partial shade, and water deeply during dry spells for the fullest, most weather-resistant flower panicles.

common_name: Pinky Winky Prime Hydrangea (Compact Improved Bicolor Panicle Hydrangea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun to partial shade; Pinky Winky Prime is a more compact, sturdier-stemmed improvement on the original Pinky Winky, needing less staking to hold its heavy bicolor flower panicles upright.

directions: Pinky Winky Prime carries the same distinctive two-tone flower panicles as the original Pinky Winky, with the lower portion of each panicle turning deep pink while the upper tip stays white, giving each flower head a bicolor effect as the bloom season progresses, on a more compact plant with stronger, more upright stems than the original cultivar. Because it blooms on new wood, it can be pruned hard in late winter without sacrificing the coming season's flowers, and its improved stem strength holds the heavy panicles upright through summer storms better than many older panicle hydrangea cultivars. Plant in moist, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun to partial shade, and water deeply during dry spells for the fullest, most colorful panicles.
